title: No News is Good News: A Critique of the One Billion Word Benchmark

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the perplexity of language models trained on Common Crawl datasets from different years (2013, 2016, 2020) on the 2011 One Billion Word Benchmark to demonstrate performance degradation due to distributional shift over time.
Qualitative evaluation and critique of the benchmark's data collection process, arguing that indiscriminately scraping news articles captures and freezes inherent media bias and factuality issues.
Qualitative critique highlighting that corpora built on news scrapes from a specific snapshot in time inherently capture the social biases and structural issues related to news reporting of that era.
